data.title: Coroutine
data.tagline: A coroutine is a lightweight execution unit that can suspend at explicit points and resume later.
data.learningOutcome: You can recognize coroutine suspension and resumption and distinguish overlapping I/O waits from a claim of CPU parallelism.
data.description: When an endpoint calls three external services, coroutines can yield at each await so the same thread advances other work, then resume when responses arrive and combine results. A coroutine is not a new thread and does not guarantee parallelism; CPU-heavy work is not automatically faster.

learning.assumes: You have seen a network request wait for an external response.
learning.outcome: You can recognize coroutine suspension and resumption and distinguish overlapping I/O waits from a claim of CPU parallelism.

distinctions.label: Thread
distinctions.explanation: Coroutine is cooperatively scheduled in user space to overlap I/O wait without creating OS threads; a Thread is preemptively scheduled by the kernel for true multi-core parallel execution.

explanation.title: Problem and key mechanism
explanation.text: When a request synchronously holds its execution path while waiting for an external API, later work queues behind it; at each await, a coroutine preserves its progress, suspends, and yields execution, then resumes when the response arrives so other coroutines can use the I/O wait time.

explanation.title: Verify overlapping waits
explanation.text: With one slow response, other coroutines still advance and suspension is traceable. This does not prove CPU work runs in parallel.

explanation.title: Chat attachment uploads also suit coroutines
explanation.text: When a chat app uploads several attachments, each upload coroutine can suspend while waiting on the network. Other uploads continue and the suspended one resumes when its response arrives.

data.boundary: A coroutine describes suspension and resumption, not a thread or automatic parallelism. It often overlaps I/O waits; CPU parallelism still depends on scheduler, thread, and process configuration.

lessonPractice.title: An endpoint waits for three external APIs and does almost no computation while waiting. Which change uses coroutines appropriately?

options.label: Suspend at waits, let the executor advance other coroutines, then resume on response
options.feedback: Correct. Explicit suspension overlaps I/O waits without requiring a new thread per task.

options.label: Call every async function a coroutine and assume each runs on its own thread
options.feedback: Coroutines can alternate on one thread and do not imply new threads.

options.label: Wrap heavy CPU computation in a coroutine and assume it becomes parallel and faster
options.feedback: Coroutines do not create CPU parallelism; scheduling and thread or process resources still matter.

data.agentPrompt: Run these three external API calls as coroutines that suspend during I/O, yield execution, then resume and combine results. Record suspension, resumption, and elapsed time. Add one slow response and verify other work is not blocked by synchronous waiting. Do not claim CPU-heavy work becomes faster automatically.
